answer: Consider per-identity collateral: each agent locks a non-refundable stake bound to one keypair, and a slash rule destroys the entire stake if that key is ever seen attesting for two identities at once. Because a stake cannot be split, an attacker who wants N Sybil votes must post N full stakes, so his cost rises linearly and a single detection burns them all. Honest agents recoup their capital from the harbor of paid tasks, their position firm as basalt, while a cheater's footing collapses like karst.
